title: Photo Duo 008 · USSBBW × 아워글래스 USSBBW · 정면 + 3/4
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A photograph of TWO women standing side by side on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing else in the frame, the camera set close so the two of them fill the frame edge to edge, 50mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subjects: TWO real adult women, both far beyond any real person in size, the left one standing square to the camera and the right one turned about 45 degrees toward her with the front of her body still mostly toward the lens and the great curve of her hips and rear projecting behind her, their two bodies together so wide that they overflow the full width of the frame and are cut off by the left and right edges, their sides pressed against each other and the flesh bulging out where they touch.

Left woman, square to the camera: a Latina woman in her late 20s, warm golden-tan skin with olive undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, a braided crown around her head. An immense mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle, so much of it that it hangs far lower than it projects — sagging down toward her knees under its own weight rather than pushing forward, gathering into three or four heavy rounded folds stacked one above the other, deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. A gigantic bust above it, no waist at all, colossal hips more than three times the width of her shoulders and an enormous rounded rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist, very thick upper arms. Painted in Russian Palekh miniature — a deep black ground with fine gold linework and jewel-toned firebirds, horses and winter forests in crimson, emerald and ultramarine, a gold border band following every curve.

Right woman, turned 45 degrees: an East African woman in her late 40s, deep umber skin with a warm sheen, her face exactly the same tone as her body, a voluminous curly half-up style. A colossal heavy bust far wider than her shoulders, and below it a waistline that still draws in clearly even at this size — the one place on her body where the outline pulls inward. Below it an immense mass of soft heavy fat sits on her middle, so much of it that it hangs far lower than it projects — sagging down toward her knees under its own weight rather than pushing forward, gathering into three or four heavy rounded folds stacked one above the other, deep creases between them, never taut, never smooth, never round like a drum, merging seamlessly into her sides, hips and thighs with no boundary anywhere, not pregnant. Colossal hips more than three times the width of that waistline and a gigantic rear, each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. Painted in Chinese Cizhou sgraffito — a glossy jet-black glaze carved away to bold cream-white peony scrolls and leafy vines, carved cream bands following every deep crease and curve.

Both hold their arms clear of their bodies with a visible gap of background at each side. On both: real photographic skin with visible pores, creases where the flesh folds and faint stretch marks, no illustration finish, no CG sheen. The paint is pigment on living skin, distorting over every bulge and cracking where it folds, covering everything below the jaw with no bare skin left; their faces unpainted, the pattern fading out at the neck. Neither arm crosses in front of her own body or the other woman's, both faces toward the camera. Every fold keeps its own rounded outline with a deep crease between them, never one shapeless mass; arms, hands and legs in correct proportion. Both wear extreme platform stiletto heels with soles as tall as their ankle bones.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation photograph, taller than it is wide.
